title: Safelight demo, re-shoot: storyboard
about: One world for the whole video: Sonoma Horizon by day and Sonoma by night, the desktop with nothing on it but Safelight's popover, and one fixed layout, the whole screen beside the popover large enough to read (the menu bar's clock with it), with no camera move while anything changes (only shot 3's left pane pulls back to both displays, and returns, while nothing does). Every shot starts and ends on the same plain afternoon screen, so each change of look is something the popover just did, never a cut. Every still is a recording composed in this layout by the real pipeline: shots 2 and 3 from drafts of their new scenes, the rest from the existing recordings, whose notes say how the re-made shot will differ. Not yet as it will be: the menu bar's clock says 21:00 in shots 1 to 4, where it will say the afternoon time shot 5 starts from.

shots.name: 1 · What it is
shots.label: Safelight
shots.what: The plain afternoon screen: Light, Safelight's popover open from the menu bar, everything off. Nothing changes; the pointer comes to rest by Color filters. The README's first sentence is the caption.

caption: Your Mac’s color filter, brightness and
Light/Dark appearance, on one schedule.

shots.name: 2 · Color filter
shots.label: Color filter
shots.what: Color filters clicked on; Intensity dragged from Low to High, and the screen goes fully red, the popover's white with it (2.2 s). Then Tint dragged once round the colours and back to red (3 s). Color filters clicked off: the plain screen again. Recorded as a draft of the new scene, color-filter.

stills.caption: Tints the whole screen
stills.small: the desktop, the menu bar, even the pointer

stills.caption: Or any other tint
stills.note: Color filters clicked off: the plain screen again, where the next shot starts.

shots.name: 3 · Brightness
shots.label: Brightness
shots.what: The left pane pulls back to both displays as they're arranged (0.6 s, before anything changes). Brightness dragged down to 40% and back up: both dim together. Adjust independently switched on, and the Dell's slider dragged down, then the Studio Display's: one at a time. Switched off again, Brightness dragged back up, both together, and the pane returns to the one screen. Recorded as a draft of the new scene, brightness.

stills.caption: Or each on its own
stills.note: Switched off, Brightness back up, the pane back on the one screen: where the next shot starts.

shots.name: 4 · Light / Dark
shots.label: Light / Dark
shots.what: Dark clicked: the menu bar and the popover change over as macOS does it (0.5 s) and the wallpaper dissolves to its night picture (2 s). Then Light clicked, and it all comes back.

stills.caption: Light or Dark in one click
Light or Dark in one click
stills.note: Re-made: then a click on Light, back to the afternoon screen.

shots.name: 5 · Schedule
shots.label: Schedule
shots.what: Schedule switched on, and the clock runs from 17:15 to 22:45, large above the screen: the filter comes on in amber and deepens, brightness falls, at 20:30 the switch to Dark plays in real time, deep dim red by 22:30. The same layout, no camera move.

stills.caption: Light and Dark switch with it

shots.name: 6 · End card (X and Shorts)
shots.what: As now: the icon, the name, “Free and open source, for Mac” and the address, faded in over the last shot. The README cut ends at 38.6 s without it.

shots.name: Shorts, 9:16
shots.what: The same shots stacked: the popover's top half above (Schedule to Brightness, where the hand is, with the menu bar's clock), the whole screen under it, the bottom fifth left empty for Shorts' own title. Shots 1, 2, 5 and the end card, about 26 s; Brightness and Light/Dark by hand are left out, as the schedule shows both.
